sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: PaddleOCR is an OCR and document AI toolkit that turns images and PDFs into text and structured data such as JSON and Markdown. It recognises text in 100+ languages and can parse tables, formulas and layouts.
sixtySeconds.problem: Getting usable data out of scanned documents, photos and complex PDFs is hard, and language models need clean text. PaddleOCR detects and recognises text and converts whole documents into structured, LLM-ready output.
whoFor: Developers building document processing or RAG pipelines
Apps that read text from photos, IDs or screens
AI agent platforms needing document parsing
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for accurate, multilingual OCR and document parsing that runs locally on CPU or GPU, with small models for edge use. It integrates with tools like Dify and RAGFlow.
requirements: An inference engine: PaddlePaddle 3.0+ or Hugging Face Transformers
Optional: an NVIDIA GPU with the matching CUDA build

overview: PaddleOCR covers two main jobs. Text recognition (PP-OCR) finds and reads text in images, including natural scenes, IDs, street views and industrial labels, with PP-OCRv6 covering 50 languages in one model in tiny, small and medium sizes. Document parsing (PaddleOCR-VL and PP-StructureV3) converts complex PDFs and images into Markdown or JSON, including tables and formulas.

You can run it from the command line or Python, with PaddlePaddle or Transformers as the inference engine. It also supports ONNX export, OpenVINO and TensorRT acceleration, multi-GPU inference, serving for other languages, and a browser SDK.

Recent releases add converting Word, Excel and PowerPoint to Markdown and exporting parsed results to DOCX. An official website offers an online experience centre and APIs if you don't want to install anything.

firstRun.title: Run OCR on an image
firstRun.code:
paddleocr ocr -i ./general_ocr_002.png \
    --use_doc_orientation_classify False \
    --use_doc_unwarping False \
    --use_textline_orientation False \
    --engine paddle

tutorial.title: Read text from an image and parse a document
tutorial.useCase: Run OCR on an image, then convert a document page to structured output.

paddleocr ocr -i ./general_ocr_002.png \
